Kirklees' population increased by around 10,800 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 430,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Kirklees increased by 2.5%, from around 422,500 in 2011 to around 433,200 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of Yorkshire and The Humber (3.7%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Kirklees was home to around 7.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 7.4 in 2011. This area was among the top 45% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Kirklees than across Yorkshire and The Humber

Median age in Kirklees

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Kirklees increased by one year, from 38 to 39 years of age.

This area had a slightly lower average (median) age than Yorkshire and The Humber as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 7,400 (an increase of 21.2%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 6,800 (7.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Ethnic groups in Kirklees

In 2021, 19.4% of Kirklees residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 16.0% in 2011. The 3.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 7.3% to 8.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 73.6% of people in Kirklees identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 79.1% in 2011), while 3.1% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.3% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.9% in 2011 to 2.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 19.4% of usual residents in Kirklees identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Kirklees

In 2021, 34.8% of Kirklees residents reported having "No religion", up from 23.9% in 2011. The rise of 10.9 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Kirklees. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 25.9% to 39.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 39.4% of people in Kirklees described themselves as Christian (down from 53.4%), while 18.5% described themselves as Muslim (up from 14.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 34.8% of usual residents in Kirklees reported having "No religion"

Kirklees residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 372,400 Kirklees residents said they were born in England. This represented 86.0% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 369,600 in 2011, which at the time represented 87.5% of Kirklees' population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with just under 18,800 Kirklees residents reporting this country of birth (4.3%). This figure was up from around 15,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 3.8% of the population of Kirklees.

The number of Kirklees residents born in India fell from just under 7,000 in 2011 (1.6% of the local population) to just under 6,700 in 2021 (1.5%).

In 2021, 86.0% of Kirklees residents reported their country of birth as England

Fewer couples without children

Kirklees saw Yorkshire and The Humber's joint second-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Richmondshire) in the proportion of households including a couple but no children (from 18.3% in 2011 to 16.5% in 2021).

Across the region, only East Riding of Yorkshire saw a greater fall in the percentage of households including a couple but no children (from 22.0% to 20.0%).

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of households including a couple but no children fell from 18.7% to 17.7%, while the percentage in nearby Calderdale fell from 18.7% to 17.2%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Kirklees decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Kirklees households, 19.1% rented privately in 2021, up from 15.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven households (14.8%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 15.3% in 2011. The percentage of Kirklees households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 67.1% to 65.5%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes in Kirklees (3.5 percentage points) was similar to the increase across Yorkshire and The Humber (3.5 percentage points, from 15.9% to 19.4%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Kirklees increased by 3.5 percentage points

Unpaid care in Kirklees

In 2021, 4.6% of Kirklees residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around 1 in 50 people (2.0%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.6% in 2011. The proportion of Kirklees residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.6% to 2.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Kirklees (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across Yorkshire and The Humber (2.7 percentage points, from 7.1% to 4.4%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Kirklees decreased by 2.7 percentage points

National identity in Kirklees

In 2021, 5.8% of Kirklees residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 4.7% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.6 percentage points, from 5.1% to 6.7%) than in Kirklees (1.1 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Kirklees increased by 1.1 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Kirklees residents aged 16 years and over, 36.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 32.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (46.0%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 48.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Kirklees that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 9.3% to 9.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Kirklees (3.8 percentage points) was similar to the increase across Yorkshire and The Humber (3.8 percentage points, from 33.9% to 37.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Kirklees increased by 3.8 percentage points

Fall in employment

Of Kirklees residents aged 16 years and over, 53.2% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 55.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.8%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.3% in 2011. The percentage of retired Kirklees residents increased from 21.2% to 21.9%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Kirklees (1.8 percentage points) than across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.1 percentage points, from 54.5% to 53.5%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Kirklees decreased by 1.8 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

In 2021, 8.9% of Kirklees residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked over 49 hours per week. This figure decreased from 11.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.9%) said they worked 15 hours or less per week, compared with 9.6% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 57.5% to 59.2%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week was greater in Kirklees (2.4 percentage points) than across Yorkshire and The Humber (2.0 percentage points, from 11.9% to 9.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.2 percentage points, from 13.3% to 11.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Kirklees decreased by 2.4 percentage points

Disability in Kirklees

In 2021, 8.0% of Kirklees residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.2%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.4% in 2011. The proportion of Kirklees residents who were not disabled increased from 79.8% to 81.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Kirklees (1.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.7 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Kirklees decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Health in Kirklees

In 2021, 44.8% of Kirklees residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 42.5% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.6% to 35.2%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Kirklees residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.3% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.1% to 4.6%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Kirklees increased by 2.3 percentage points
